task.title: Reject cross-origin and foreign-Host requests on the web board
task.description:
The local web board accepts requests from any website while `workbook serve` runs. Verified empirically against a throwaway repo at commit c453596 with the server on 127.0.0.1:7399:

- `GET /api/tasks` with `Host: evil.example:7399` returned HTTP 200 and the full task list. There is no Host allowlist, so DNS rebinding grants a hostile page same-origin access to every route.
- `POST /api/tasks` with `Origin: https://evil.example` and `Content-Type: application/json` returned 200 and created a task.
- `POST /api/tasks` with `Content-Type: text/plain` returned 200 and created a task. text/plain is a CORS simple request, so this needs no preflight and no rebinding: it works from any site via a plain HTML form while the board is running.

After the three requests the store contained the seed task plus "INJECTED VIA CROSS ORIGIN" and "CSRF TEXT PLAIN PWN".

`serveHTTP` (internal/webui/handler.go:243-256) sets CSP and nosniff, checks path shape and method, and performs no origin, Host, or Content-Type validation. `decodeRequest` (internal/webui/handler.go:678-691) decodes any body as JSON regardless of Content-Type. PATCH/PUT/DELETE are protected only incidentally, by requiring a preflight that never succeeds; POST has no such protection.

Impact is worse than ordinary CSRF for this project. Board mutations publish through boardPublisher, so an injected task synchronizes to origin, reaches every teammates clone, and is later read by coding agents as work instructions. That makes a drive-by web page a prompt-injection channel into the agent loop. The default port is fixed at 127.0.0.1:7331 (internal/cli/run.go:809), so the target is trivially guessable.

Acceptance:
- Requests whose Host header is not the bound loopback host and port are rejected.
- Requests carrying an Origin header that is not the servers own origin are rejected.
- Mutating routes require Content-Type: application/json and reject the three CORS form-safe types.
- Regression tests cover each rejection, including the text/plain form-POST shape and a foreign Host on a GET.
- Binding a non-loopback --addr prints a clear warning that the board has no authentication.
